These components represent underlying constructs such as overall game efficacy, raising efficacy, and backcourt play efficacy. Each component is a linear combination of original variables weighted by loadings. This allows for dimensionality reduction without loss of essential information. The dual nature of these components—both descriptive and predictive—enables Bayesian updating of player effectiveness given new data. The failure mode occurs when variance explained drops below 70%, suggesting insufficient latent structure. The interplay between these components and the three game phases creates a dynamic system where situational awareness and tactical adaptation are encoded in both static and temporal dimensions. The anthropological fitness kernel provides a foundational constraint on how these latent structures manifest physically, forming a closed-loop system of performance optimization.
